key_points: MCAO is defined as ≥50% narrowing of a central airway (trachea, mainstem bronchi, bronchus intermedius, or lobar bronchi) by malignancy.
Therapeutic bronchoscopy under general anesthesia is the backbone of multimodality management and bridges to definitive oncologic therapy.
Classifying obstruction as intrinsic, extrinsic, or mixed guides modality selection and prognosis.
Airway stents palliate extrinsic compression and maintain patency after debridement but require careful follow-up and removal once tumor regresses.
For immediate-effect ablation, reduce FiO2 to ≤0.4 and keep probe tips away from flammable devices to decrease airway fire risk.

clinical_procedures.name: Therapeutic bronchoscopy planning and anesthesia
steps: Perform comprehensive airway-focused preassessment (mouth opening >3 finger breadths, teeth status, modified Mallampati, neck mobility >90°, thyromental distance >3 finger breadths).
Plan anesthesia with general anesthesia/deep sedation and paralytics for therapeutic bronchoscopy; coordinate with anesthesiology.
Select ventilatory support (jet ventilation or controlled/spontaneous assisted ventilation) based on local expertise and patient status; consider ECMO standby for critical obstructions.
notes: General anesthesia/deep sedation with paralytics is associated with fewer complications than moderate sedation.
Either jet or controlled ventilation is acceptable during therapeutic bronchoscopy.

clinical_procedures.name: Tumor debridement and immediate-effect ablation
steps: Debulk endobronchial tumor using rigid or flexible forceps; consider rigid bronchoscope bevel for coring proximal tumors.
Apply immediate-effect ablative modalities (electrocautery probes, snare/knife; APC; laser) to achieve hemostasis and vaporize tumor.
Maintain FiO2 ≤0.4 and keep active probe tip away from flammable devices to reduce airway fire risk.
notes: Cryoprobe-assisted debridement can improve efficiency versus forceps.
Rigid bronchoscopy offers technical advantages for proximal, bulky lesions; flexible scope adjunct is common.

clinical_procedures.name: Delayed-effect local therapies
steps: Consider photodynamic therapy (PDT) to reduce tumor regrowth in appropriate candidates.
Recognize that brachytherapy and cryotherapy have limited current utilization in many centers.
notes: After PDT, advise strict photosensitivity precautions (avoid sunlight up to 8 weeks).
Monitor for airway stenosis as a potential PDT complication.

clinical_procedures.name: Airway stenting
steps: Use silicone or fully covered hybrid metallic stents to palliate extrinsic compression or maintain patency after debridement in endobronchial CAO.
Prescribe mucociliary clearance therapy (e.g., nebulized hypertonic saline or acetylcysteine) to prevent mucus plugging.
Follow closely and remove stents once significant tumor regression occurs; choose routine or symptom-driven bronchoscopy; use CT to assess stent patency.
notes: Complications include granulation tissue, migration, mucus plugging, and rarely erosion (risk increased near periprocedural radiation).
Silicone stents require rigid bronchoscopy for deployment.

clinical_procedures.name: Integration with oncologic therapy
steps: Use bronchoscopic palliation to bridge to definitive chemoradiation and/or surgery.

For EBRT in central tumors and in patients with stents, coordinate multidisciplinary planning and adjust dose to minimize toxicity; avoid concurrent chemo-EBRT in high-risk cases and remove stents when feasible.
notes: Therapeutic bronchoscopy can facilitate liberation from mechanical ventilation in selected MCAO patients.

treatment_algorithms.title: Suggested algorithm for the management of malignant central airway obstruction
specific_recommendations: If non-surgical: debridement/ablation of endobronchial tumor.
Stent placement for extrinsic obstruction or tumor recurrence after debridement.
Consider local bronchoscopic therapy (PDT, brachytherapy, cryotherapy) to prevent regrowth.
Systemic chemotherapy plus external beam radiation as indicated.
decision_points_and_pathways: Non-surgical Candidate → Debridement/Ablation → Stent Placement → Local Bronchoscopic Therapy → Systemic Chemotherapy + EBRT.
treatment_algorithms.source_excerpt: Fig. 5 Suggested algorithm for the management of malignant central airway obstruction…

clinical_guidelines.title: ACCP guideline: Rigid over flexible bronchoscopy for therapeutic interventions
specific_recommendations: Use rigid bronchoscopy over flexible bronchoscopy for therapeutic interventions in central airway obstruction.
Flexible bronchoscope is adjunctive for distal/smaller lesions; silicone stents require rigid bronchoscopy.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: …ACCP guidelines… suggested rigid over flexible bronchoscopy…

clinical_guidelines.title: ACCP guideline: Anesthetic approach for therapeutic bronchoscopy
specific_recommendations: Use general anesthesia/deep sedation with paralytics for therapeutic bronchoscopy.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: …use of general anesthesia/deep sedation with paralytics…

clinical_guidelines.title: ACCP guideline: Ventilator support during therapeutic bronchoscopy under general anesthesia
specific_recommendations: Use either jet ventilation or controlled/spontaneous assisted ventilation for therapeutic bronchoscopy under general anesthesia.

clinical_guidelines.title: Safety recommendations for immediate-effect ablative therapies
specific_recommendations: Decrease FiO2 to ≤0.4 during ablative therapies.
Keep active tip away from flammable devices.
decision_points_and_pathways: Before activating ablative device → reduce FiO2 to ≤0.4 and ensure safe tip positioning.
clinical_guidelines.monitoring_requirements: Monitor oxygen concentration and device-tip position.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: …decrease the fraction of inhaled oxygen (FiO2) to ≤0.4…

clinical_guidelines.title: ACCP recommendations: Airway stents for MCAO (indications and follow-up)
specific_recommendations: Consider airway stents for extrinsic compression or after debridement when prior therapy failed.
Either routine surveillance or symptom-driven bronchoscopy is acceptable after stent placement.
Use CT chest to assess stent patency; remove stents once tumor regression is evident.
clinical_guidelines.monitoring_requirements: Careful follow-up with bronchoscopy and CT.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: …airway stents should be considered… CT chest can be utilized… remove stents as soon as feasible…

clinical_guidelines.title: Recommendations for EBRT in patients with MCAO and airway stents
specific_recommendations: Carefully plan radiation and adjust dose to minimize toxicity.
Avoid concurrent chemotherapy and EBRT in high-risk patients.
Remove airway stents as soon as feasible in high-risk settings.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with central airway tumors, particularly with stents and high risk for complications.
clinical_guidelines.contraindications_and_exceptions: Concurrent chemotherapy and EBRT should be avoided in high-risk patients.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: …avoid concurrent chemotherapy and EBRT… stents should be removed as soon as feasible.

definitions.definition: Malignant central airway obstruction; ≥50% narrowing of trachea, mainstem bronchi, bronchus intermedius, or lobar bronchi by malignancy.
Tumor within the airway lumen causing obstruction.
Photodynamic therapy; delayed-effect local therapy with photosensitivity precautions.
Argon plasma coagulation; noncontact thermal ablation modality.
External beam radiation therapy; careful planning needed in central tumors, especially with stents.
Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation; possible bridge for anesthesia in severe airway obstruction.

clinical_pearls.content: Visualization of a patent distal airway predicts higher chance of successful bronchoscopic relief and more favorable outcomes.
Early therapeutic bronchoscopy is associated with improved survival and palliation; act promptly when feasible.
Reduce FiO2 to ≤0.4 and keep ablative probe tips away from flammable equipment to mitigate airway fire risk.

references.citation: Mahmood K, Frazer-Green L, Gonzalez AV, et al. Management of central airway obstruction: an American College of Chest Physicians Clinical Practice Guideline. Chest. 2024;167(1):283–95.

clinical_applications.content: Therapeutic bronchoscopy is central to palliation and as a bridge to definitive therapy in MCAO.

practice_recommendations.content: Use multimodality bronchoscopic therapy under general anesthesia; reduce FiO2 to ≤0.4 during ablation.

problems_observed.finding: Wide variation in MCAO management across institutions and specialties
problems_observed.details: Clinical practice varies widely, associated with poorer outcomes.

guideline_adherence.implication: Implement guideline-based, multidisciplinary management to improve outcomes.

points: MCAO occurs in ~13–17% of contemporary lung cancer cohorts and carries high symptom burden with poor prognosis.
Definition: ≥50% narrowing of trachea, mainstem bronchi, bronchus intermedius, or lobar bronchi.
Multimodality therapeutic bronchoscopy with multidisciplinary coordination improves palliation, enables definitive therapy, and can improve survival.
